overall: The AG found the complaint timely, found the January 21 litigation executive session notice insufficiently detailed and untimely approval of its executive session minutes a violation, deemed the minutes violation intentional, and ordered compliance and member training.

allegations.summary: Board argued the complaint was untimely and should be dismissed; the AG found it was filed within 30 days of reasonable discovery.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, filing an Open Meeting Law complaint regarding an insufficiently detailed notice for a cancelled executive session would have seemed futile.

allegations.summary: Executive session notice for a January 21 meeting said only 'discussion of litigation strategy' without identifying the litigation matter.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to identify which litigation matter would be discussed.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board falsely stated that no executive session was held on January 21; the letter does not separately rule on this claim.
allegations.key_passage: Ms. Munford understood this statement to mean that no executive session had taken place on January 21.

allegations.summary: Chair threatened to clear the room if outbursts occurred; the AG considered whether the open session was closed to the public.
allegations.key_passage: As the January 21 meeting remained open to the public, we find no violation

allegations.summary: Board did not approve its January 21 executive session minutes in a timely manner; they remained unapproved months later.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to approve meeting minutes for its January 21 executive session in a timely manner.

allegations.summary: Complainant urged that the untimely approval of executive session minutes was intentional, given the Board's prior OML determination on the same issue.
allegations.key_passage: As the Board has again failed to approve meeting minute in a timely manner for a meeting held almost exactly a year after that determination was issued, we find the Board’s violation to be intentional.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
All members of the Board must attend an Open Meeting Law training webinar provided by the AG's office within ninety (90) days of receipt of the letter
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution the Board that a determination by our office of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law. Furthermore, we order all members of the Board to attend an Open Meeting Law training webinar provided by our office within ninety (90) days of the Board’s receipt of this letter.
